title: Token Railroad: Lattice view for per-token cost allocation, export, and pricing patterns
creator: Aisha Khatri
description: Problem: Customers and internal teams need a compact, actionable way to trace per-token cost back to the routes/models/sessions that generated them and to export reconciliable line items for chargebacks. Existing token cost panels (heatmaps, ledgers) are useful but either too aggregated or too verbose for rapid triage. Goal: Design a novel "Token Railroad" lattice UI that surfaces token-level attribution lanes (tracks) across dimensions (route, model, user/team, prompt template), shows token density and pricing slab mapping, supports role-aware exports (CSV/Parquet) that map to billing SKUs, and integrates pricing pattern suggestions for common chargeback workflows.
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity Token Railroad mockups for desktop and tablet exist in Figma with annotated interactions
Prototype supports: lane collapse/expand, token-range scrubber, hover drill to tokens -> origin request/PR, and export button that pre-fills CSV schema
Export schemas (CSV & Parquet) documented and confirmed by Billing/Finance and Platform Eng to be mappable to existing invoice line-items
PM and two engineers have reviewed feasibility notes and flagged at most two implementation blockers (spike tasks created)
Usability test (5 sessions) shows users can identify top 3 cost drivers for a sample account within 90s using the lattice
design_notes: Lattice metaphor: horizontal tracks = attribution dimension (route/model/team), vertical axis = time or grouped buckets, tokens represented as compressed beads sized by token-count and colored by pricing slab
Two primary modes: Overview (compact density lanes + top contributors) and Inspect (expanded lane with per-request tokens, prompt preview, cost tooltip)

Pricing patterns: slab overlay that visualizes current pricing bands (free tier, per-token slabs, reserved rates). Allow toggle to view effective unit price vs base price to communicate discounts/reservations

Export: include role-aware columns (viewer vs billing-admin). Default CSV columns: timestamp, route, model, session_id, user_id (anonymized), prompt_hash, tokens_in, tokens_out, effective_unit_price, cost_usd, billing_sku, note. Provide Parquet for bulk reconciliation
Interactions: scrubber for time zoom, marquee to select multiple beads and create an ad-hoc allocation group, inline `Assign to` action to save allocation to a cost center
Performance: use progressive rendering (canvas for beads) and server-side pre-aggregation for wide time ranges. Fallback to aggregated sparkline if >500k beads
Accessibility: colorblind-safe palette, keyboard navigation for lanes, tooltips available via focus, CSV export respects locale for decimals
review_feedback: PM (Sofia Morales): Like the lattice metaphor for rapid triage. Request that exported CSV include a `billing_reason` free-text column so finance can attach customer-facing notes.
Eng (Liam Chen): Concern about per-request bead rendering at large scales. Suggest server-side delta aggregation and a client sampling strategy. Spike ticket proposed ENG-824800.
Billing (Priya Desai): Confirmed CSV schema maps to invoice lines but asked for optional `customer_sku` column for enterprise accounts with custom contracted SKUs.

Design lead (Ravi Patel): Recommend a compact baseline layout for usage in the Console sidebar and full-screen Inspect for deep dives. Ask to run A/B of slab overlay vs numeric-only legend in usability testing
decisions: Adopt lattice/rail metaphor as primary visual, but include alternative table-first view for low-visibility use cases
Export CSV & Parquet supported; CSV is default for quick share, Parquet for bulk reconciliation with Finance
Server-side pre-aggregation required for >24h ranges to avoid client overload (ENG spike before implementation)
Include an "Assign to cost center" quick action in Inspect mode that creates a cost allocation tag via API endpoint (integration story with ENG-48201)
Pricing slab overlay remains opt-in by default to avoid visual noise for new users
next_steps: Finalize hi-fi frames and handoff spec to Eng (owner: Marco) by 2026-03-21
Create ENG spike ENG-824800 to validate rendering approach and server-side pre-aggregation by 2026-03-18
Sync with Billing to lock export schema and `customer_sku` handling by 2026-03-20
Run 5 moderated usability sessions (mix of platform engineers, finance analysts, product managers) and iterate on slab overlay visibility settings
